q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: SELECT DISTINCT NAME FROM SALESPERSON WHERE SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O LEFT JOIN COMPANY C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE C.NAME = 'RED')
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT NAME FROM SALESPERSON WHERE SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O LEFT JOIN COMPANY C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE C.NAME = 'RED')
explanation: Both queries aim to find the names of salespersons who have not sold any products from the company named 'RED'. They achieve this by checking the absence of orders from 'RED' in the salesperson's order history.
